supported_source_facts: Mesa native-fence creation flushes with ST_FLUSH_FENCE_FD; it does not request the separate ST_FLUSH_WAIT completion branch.

Mesa virgl zero-initializes EXECBUFFER, so this public source path sets no input/output timeline syncobj arrays. A native input FD is attached only when cbuf.in_fence_fd>=0; server_sync accumulates external fences and skips non-external fences.
Kernel input-fence waiting skips fences matching the submission context. This is an ordering optimization already present, not an omitted shortcut demonstrated by the capture.

Kernel submission includes buffer/command allocation and user copies, optional input dependencies, buffer reservation locking, and queue submission. The boundary measurement does not distinguish those suboperations or scheduling.

The control queue releases its queue spinlock, notifies the host, then waits for enough descriptor space before retrying. Fence sequence assignment occurs only after queue position is known, and buffer reservations/fences are attached in that ordering.
Output sync_file FD installation follows job enqueue. This path does not explicitly wait for its own output fence to complete.
The separately measured WAIT ioctl is a distinct reservation-completion operation; its existence does not identify the cause inside the long EXECBUFFER call.
